app.name: Rowtine
app.baseline: Your knitting and crochet projects over time.

onboarding.swipeHint: Swipe right to go back. And when a row of tabs or categories runs off the screen — in a project, in the library — drag it with your finger, from right to left.
onboarding.welcomeBody: Everything is ready. Two projects and a few sample patterns are waiting for you: open them to see how the app works, and add your first skeins to your Yarn stash. Wander through the menus and screens to get familiar with the interface — that's what these samples are for.

calc.title: Stitch calculator
calc.currentHint: How many stitches you currently have on the needle.
calc.targetHint: How many stitches you want after the increases or decreases.
calc.rowsHint: How many rows to spread the increases/decreases over, evenly.
calc.cadenceHintInc: How often you work them. If your pattern says “8 increases every 2 rows”, this is the 2.
calc.cadenceHintDec: How often you work them. If your pattern says “8 decreases every 2 rows”, this is the 2.
calc.rowsHintRound: How many rounds to spread the increases/decreases over, evenly.
calc.cadenceHintIncRound: How often you work them. If your pattern says “8 increases every 2 rounds”, this is the 2.
calc.cadenceHintDecRound: How often you work them. If your pattern says “8 decreases every 2 rounds”, this is the 2.
calc.lengthDetailInc: {n} increase in all, one {every}. | {n} increases in all, one {every}.
calc.lengthDetailDec: {n} decrease in all, one {every}. | {n} decreases in all, one {every}.
calc.fillInLength: Fill in the fields to see the number of {unit}.
calc.perTimeHintInc: How many stitches you add at once. Usually 1; 2 for a sleeve, where you increase one stitch on each side; 8 for a raglan that increases at all four corners.
calc.perTimeHintDec: How many stitches you take off at once. Usually 1; 2 for a sleeve, where you decrease one stitch on each side; 8 for a raglan that decreases at all four corners.
calc.notExactInc: Your target can’t be reached exactly by adding {s} stitches each time.
calc.notExactDec: Your target can’t be reached exactly by removing {s} stitches each time.
calc.mismatch: Target doesn’t match the mode: for increases the target must be higher than the current stitches, for decreases lower.
calc.fillIn: Fill in the fields to see the distribution.

needleGauge.labelNeedleHint: The needle (or hook) size shown on the label for this gauge.
needleGauge.labelStitchesHint: The stitch count shown on the yarn label.
needleGauge.targetStitchesHint: The stitch count required by the pattern.
needleGauge.fillIn: Fill in at least the needle size and the stitch counts (label + pattern) to see a recommendation.
needleGauge.sameGauge: Your yarn already gives the right gauge at this size: no need to change.
needleGauge.resultSame: The nearest standard size stays {mm} mm — the difference is too small to change size.
needleGauge.outOfRange: This difference falls outside common sizes: this yarn is probably not a good match for this pattern, whatever needle size you use.
needleGauge.rowNote: Heads up: the row trend doesn't match the stitch trend — even after adjusting, your row count may still differ from the pattern.
needleGauge.caveat: This size is a starting point, not a guarantee: yarns don't all react the same way to a needle size change. Knit a swatch at this size to check before you start.

icounter.title: Counter
icounter.addShapingHint: E.g. a sleeve: count rows and track increases/decreases as you go.
icounter.addRepeatHint: E.g. “repeat rows 1 to 8, 5 times”: counts the row blocks.

importLocal.title: Import a PDF
importLocal.lead: The pattern is parsed on your device: free, offline, faithful to the PDF.
importLocal.leadNext: The pattern is saved straight into your library; you'll be able to fix the sections afterwards if needed.
importLocal.waitingSync: Syncing your library, the import will start as soon as it's done…
importLocal.correctHint: You'll be able to fix the section categorisation from inside the pattern.
importLocal.scanned: This PDF looks scanned: it holds no readable text, so the app cannot extract anything from it. Enter the pattern by hand, or write to us at {email} — we can help you prepare it.
importLocal.doneCaveat: The conversion is never perfect: read the pattern through before you follow it. Everything can be fixed in the app.
importLocal.blockColumns: This PDF looks laid out in more than 2 columns: the extracted text will be scrambled.
importLocal.blockMultiPattern: This file looks like it contains several patterns (or a book): only one pattern can be imported at a time.
importLocal.blockLead: Automatic import was paused. You can import it anyway, but it will likely need significant correction.

importCaveat.title: An imported pattern needs a read-through
importCaveat.body: The app reads your PDF on its own. It gets things wrong sometimes: a skipped row, two sizes mixed up, a badly split table. Always read an imported pattern through before you follow it. Everything can be fixed in the app.

importZip.noMd: This zip contains no pattern file (.md). Check the file.

help.title: How to correct the pattern
help.steps1: Tap “Edit text” to fix badly split sentences or misidentified lines.
help.steps2: Select one or more lines, then say what they are for using the toolbar.
help.stripsTitle: The strips at the bottom of the screen
help.stripDiagrams: Diagrams: the list of the pattern's charts. You can change a chart's tracking type, rename it, turn it back into a plain image, or send it to the gallery.
help.stripGallery: Pattern gallery: the images that come with the pattern without being in the text. You can add some (camera, file, PDF page), remove some, or turn one into a chart.
help.stripImageTap: In the text, tap an image to follow it as a chart, change its type, or turn it back into a plain image.
help.tagsCol2: What it becomes in your project
help.tagRang: A checkbox to tick as you knit.
help.tagCompteur: A repeated step, with its counter. Repeat = work the line N times. Cadence = work the line every X rows, N times.
help.tagSection: A part heading, with its icon (Body, Sleeve…).
help.tagReference: Information for the pattern sheet (yarn, needles, sizes…) — not for tracking.
help.refsIntro: These blocks fill in the pattern sheet. They are not used for row-by-row tracking.
help.refTips: Practical tips or advice, one per line.
help.refAbbreviations: The list of abbreviations, one per line.
help.refMeasurements: The table of finished measurements, one row per measurement. Not per-size instructions: those are Sections.
help.sections: Pick the part of the pattern the line opens. The name becomes a title in your project, with its icon. If none fits: Text.
help.markupTag: the braces carry the category marker, always in English. Don’t translate it: the app would no longer recognise it, and the block would drop out of your project’s reference sheet.
help.markupSubtitle: a subheading, inside a Techniques block.
help.markupSyntaxIntro: At the start of a line:

safOnboarding.title: Welcome!
safOnboarding.body: Rowtine needs a folder on your phone to work. Pick one: if it isn't already named “Rowtine” and doesn't already contain your data, your data will live in a “Rowtine” subfolder, created if needed.
safOnboarding.failed: This folder could not be prepared. Please choose another one.
safOnboarding.changeBody: Choose the folder where Rowtine will store your data. If it isn't already named “Rowtine” and doesn't already contain your data, your data will live in a “Rowtine” subfolder, created if needed.

restore.foundOnDevice: Rowtine data was found in this folder.
restore.discardHint: You can bring them back into the app, or start from scratch — the folder's data will then be lost.
restore.discardDone: The data on this device has replaced the data in the folder.
restore.welcomeBody: Everything you had saved in this folder has been found. Happy knitting!

restoreFailure.errorBody: A technical error occurred while restoring your data. The details are shown below; you can copy them to report the problem.
restoreFailure.unownedBody: Your data has been restored, but taking over the folder could not be confirmed: saving your Rowtine data stays paused.

versionGuard.title: A newer version wrote this data
versionGuard.message: This device holds data written by a newer version of the app. Everything this version of the app recognises stays readable and goes into the automatic backup. But the app is not in the state it expects, and that will not sort itself out. To start again from a sound database: first check that your backup is really present in the designated folder, then clear the app's data and restore it from that folder.
